svg.title: Tabby AI Tools v0.9.4 interface illustration — Markdown replies, terminal tools, local login and API connections
svg.desc: Tabby AI Tools v0.9.4 shared Agent question navigation: hover or focus to preview, click to jump. Centered compact 1px lines share an 18px right strip with a draggable conversation scrollbar; previews open left and there is no left gutter; theme-aware up/down buttons appear on overflow. Green indicates completion; pale green indicates ordinary interruption. Blue indicates running or external prerequisites; red indicates user Stop or unfinished/limited work. Turns with no known execution result remain neutral; overall goal completion is separate. Markdown output: assistant tables preserve column alignment, code blocks have syntax highlighting and copy buttons and wide content scrolls inside messages. Codex checks known Windows companions and recovers once at an idle boundary without replay; Claude rechecks its original CLI selector before every invocation; native Linux SSH agents use an independent PID and output-only PTY identity proof; clipboard attachments with clickable thumbnails and larger image previews and native tab progress; custom instructions/private CLI session spaces and Pi configuration: native provider search, offline SDK 1.4.0 catalog, four custom protocols and Save/Discard/Copy drafts. Interface illustration, not a running screenshot. Windows default Codex discovery compares actual CLI versions across PATH and desktop/standalone installations; a stable directory limits selection to its own children. Commands and multiline workflow scripts retain up to 10,000 characters; explicit AI decision steps return to scripted execution after judgment. Conditional recordings preserve interaction intent; local rules run first, with an optional current-connection helper model and rebind-before-resume checkpoints. Settings use two-row connection cards and editor summaries, compact headings and full-page scrolling for connections, workflows/preferences and scheduled tasks, with no fixed-height editor. The assistant sidebar coordinates example staging database and application terminals. Connection and model controls share one compact row. Scheduled tasks, provider connections, startup opening enabled by default and twelve interface languages and the Claude Code local-login connection are shown below. Active goals continue automatically by default. Thinking and tool calls appear as collapsed conversation entries that can be expanded. Terminal reads return early after reliable shell completion. Terminal output is read on demand without automatic forwarding; an example health table and a copyable code block are shown. Archive status distinguishes successful checkpoints from successful persistence. Pi runtime settings show the built-in runtime and an optional Node override, host-only tools and opt-in automatic context compaction. The provider list includes Kimi and Alibaba Cloud Coding Plan connections. Custom OpenAI-compatible settings show an example Base URL, model, protocol and authentication. Compact navigation UI with optional Pi SDK runtime, built-in Node 22.19+, manual context compaction and structured retry waiting.
